title: The Lead Verification Checklist: Scan Every Lead Before You Send
description: The lead verification checklist from the reel: what to check, which results to remove, the tools to use and how to keep bounces under 2%.
lead: This is the full lead verification checklist from the reel. Every lead gets scanned before a single email goes out. Here's what to check, what to remove, which tools to use, and the bounce rate to aim for.
insider: Every client list we send to gets verified first. That's how one client sent **96,408 emails in 5 days with a 0.45% bounce rate** and booked 25 calls that week. The checklist is the easy part. Building the right list, cleaning it and watching bounces every day is the work we do for clients.

blocks.text: Why you scan before you send

Some addresses on every list are bad: typos, people who left the company, dead inboxes. When you send to them, the email bounces. Lots of bounces tell inbox providers you don't know who you're emailing, and your sender reputation drops. Then even your good emails start landing in spam.

[Hunter's 2026 report](https://hunter.io/the-state-of-cold-email), based on 31 million emails, found an average bounce rate of **3.6%**, usually caused by unverified contact data. [Instantly's 2026 benchmark report](https://instantly.ai/cold-email-benchmark-report-2026) says to keep bounces **below 2%, ideally much lower**, and to verify before sending.

blocks.text: Hunter notes that bounces usually come from unverified contact data, but they can also come from a low sender reputation or sending too fast. Scanning fixes the first cause; a proper warm-up and slow ramp fix the others.

items: **Remove duplicates.** The same person twice means two emails and double the risk.
**Fix obvious typos** like gmial.com or missing dots.
**Remove role-based addresses** like info@, admin@ and support@.

**Run the full list through a verifier** like [Hunter Email Verifier](https://hunter.io/email-verifier), [NeverBounce](https://neverbounce.com), [ZeroBounce](https://www.zerobounce.net) or [Instantly's verification](https://instantly.ai/email-verification).
**Keep only valid** addresses in your main campaign.
**Put catch-all addresses aside.** If you use them, send in a small separate batch and watch bounces closely.
**Check the right person.** A valid email for the wrong job title is still a wasted send. Spot-check 20 leads on LinkedIn or the company website.
**Re-verify old lists.** If a list is more than a few months old, scan it again. People change jobs.

blocks.label: Verify close to send day
blocks.text: Verify right before a campaign starts, not months before. Lists go stale as people move jobs.

items: Without scanning, at Hunter's 3.6% average: 2,000 × 3.6% = **72 bounces**.
Instantly's limit is under 2%: 2,000 × 2% = **40 bounces max**.
Say the scan removes 150 invalid, role-based and duplicate addresses and sets aside 100 catch-alls. You're left with **1,750 valid leads**.
Aim for under 1%: 1,750 × 1% = **under 18 bounces**. Our 5-day blitz client ran at 0.45%.
Check the bounce rate every day for the first week.
If it goes over 2%, **pause** that campaign.
Find which part of the list is bouncing (one source or one company type is usually the cause).

Re-verify, remove the bad leads and restart slowly. [Google's sender guidelines](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126) also say to lower volume when messages start bouncing, then increase slowly.

blocks.label: AI prompt: clean a lead list
blocks.text:
I have a lead list as a CSV with these columns: [list columns].
My ideal buyer is: [job title, industry, company size].

Give me step-by-step instructions (Google Sheets formulas are fine) to:
1. Remove duplicate emails.
2. Flag role-based addresses (info@, sales@, admin@, support@, hello@).
3. Flag rows where the job title doesn't match my buyer.
4. Prepare the cleaned list for upload to an email verification tool.
Keep it simple.
